_WHAT_THIS_IS: TEMPLATE ONLY. This is NOT an authorization and it is NOT a valid manifest as it stands. CMB-RP1 does not exist, is not designed, and is not approved. This file exists so that whoever builds CMB-RP1 does not have to invent the shape under time pressure.
_WHY_IT_CANNOT_ACCIDENTALLY_CLEAR_ANYTHI: The filename ends in .TEMPLATE.json, so it is not the checker's default manifest.
source_commit is a placeholder, not 40 hex characters.
config_digest is empty and will not match, which the checker reports as an authority failure and blocks on.
derivation is 'derived_from_pipeline_config', so the checker REFUSES unless --pipeline-config is supplied and agrees.
_HOW_TO_MAKE_IT_REAL: 1. The CMB-RP1 launcher EMITS a pipeline config recording whether replayed memories actually enter training batches. It must be emitted by the pipeline, never hand-written.
2. The launcher DERIVES memory_feeds_training from that config -- it does not declare it.
3. Fill deployment-time fields: job_id, source_commit (the real tip), timestamp, declared_owner.
4. Recompute config_digest = sha256 over all non-underscore keys except config_digest itself, sorted.
5. Run the trigger with --expected-scope DEVELOPMENT_REPLAY --job-id CMB-RP1 --pipeline-config <emitted> --receipt-out <path>.
6. Abort on exit 5, 10, 20 or 30. Bind the trigger receipt and manifest digest into the run receipt.
_flag_note: CMB-RP0 measured memory_feeds_training=true for the bench, because replayed memories were mixed into training batches. CMB-RP1 is expected to be the same. This value must be DERIVED from the emitted pipeline config, not trusted from this file.
